test_policy.notes: Applicants must submit ACT/SAT scores or a personal statement ('it is your choice, but one must be submitted'). Admission is rolling.

requirements.notes: The St. Mary's application, ApplyTexas, Common App and Coalition App are all accepted free of charge. Required: application, high school transcript, and either test scores or a personal statement; one recommendation letter and a resume are optional. International applicants submit the application plus official high school transcripts (scratch card information for West African exam countries). The Common Data Set rates GPA very important, and rigor, test scores, essay, extracurriculars, character and volunteer work important.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Exempt: applicants with a US high school diploma or a degree from an accredited US institution, a bachelor's or equivalent from a non-US university in a country where English is the main language of instruction, and citizens of listed countries (e.g. Canada except Quebec, UK, Australia, Nigeria); waivers are decided case by case, and AP/IB and other curricula may be considered in place of tests. Scores must be within six months of the application date and come directly from the testing agency. Applicants without the scores can take the Intensive English Program (online, about $1,350 per course plus a $100 deposit; needs B1 level and an iTEP placement test); the pages do not describe a conditional-admission route for undergraduates.

english.notes: The pages do not list a minimum for the new 1-6 TOEFL.
110 or higher for undergraduates (graduate minimum is 115).

aid.notes: First-time freshmen who apply by Feb. 1 and enroll full-time are automatically considered for academic merit scholarships of $10,000-$26,000 per year; the page does not say whether international students are eligible. The Global Scholars Program gives international students $2,000 per year for academic excellence and cultural understanding (renewed annually). The university reports that nearly 98% of first-time freshmen receive scholarships or institutional grants. Common Data Set: 55 nonresidents received institutional aid, average $42,263.
